question.worked_solution:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $\sqrt{3w}-\sqrt{2}.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{3w}-\sqrt{2},$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{3w}+\sqrt{2}} & = \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{3w}+\sqrt{2}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3w}-\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3w}-\sqrt{2}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{3w}-\sqrt{2})}{(\sqrt{3w}+\sqrt{2})(\sqrt{3w}-\sqrt{2})} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{3w}-\sqrt{2}}{(\sqrt{3w})^{2}-(\sqrt{2})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{3w}-\sqrt{2}}{3w-2}\end{aligned}
$$
